audio.production_requirements: Follow Diagnostic Bible 6.1 and 6.1.1 and the existing Listening production record format (docs/ielts/practice/LISTENING_EXTENSION_02_DRAFT.json): assemble the segments in order with the spoken copyright notice first in the instruction voice; insert real silence (30 seconds after the reading instruction, 15 seconds after the passage) and verify it in the encoded file; clean natural speech with no added noise, phone effect or music; no clipping; record provider, model, voice identities, settings, script SHA-256, measured pauses, duration and delivered SHA-256; never overwrite an approved file. Human review covers sound, transcript fidelity (every number, correction and name), speaker distinctness, keys and device playback, each recorded separately. Generated-voice licence and distribution rights remain an open gate, as for existing tracks.

prerequisites: Lessons 1 and 3 strategies: wait for the final detail and respect word limits. Late joiners use the catch-up sheet from the Lesson 2 pack, which covers the Lesson 1 correction strategy.
Teacher has checked actual Listening Screener and review states privately. Completed screeners are reused by reference; missing ones are arranged outside this lesson.
Approved recordings IELTS-05-L1 and IELTS-05-L2 exist with verified hashes. Without them this lesson is not releasable; see Plan B.

objectives.text: Recognise three distractor patterns: a corrected detail, a rejected option and a changed or contrasting opinion.
Match spoken paraphrases to the words in a question before and while listening.
Track who holds which view in a three-speaker academic discussion.

levels.foundation: Answer-type hints beside each gap; teacher-controlled second play with a pause after each answer, recorded as support.
levels.core: Complete each recording once under practice conditions, then explain each answer with the words heard.
levels.extension: For each multiple-choice item, write the exact words that made one wrong option tempting.
levels.high_band: Identify the discourse signal for every change of plan or view (but, actually, in that case, I'm not sure) and predict where a trap will appear before the second recording begins.

blocks.title: Three traps in one sentence
blocks.mode: Teacher-led mini-model; read aloud live from the slide
blocks.instructions: Listen to your teacher read each short line once. Write the final answer only.

stimulus.title: Mini-model lines (teacher reads aloud)
paragraphs: A: Can we meet on Tuesday? B: I have a lecture then. Let's say Thursday.
A: The library is noisy, so let's not work there. The café upstairs is quieter.
A: I thought the first article was the most useful. B: Really? I found the second one far clearer, and that's the one I'll use.

items.evidence: Let's say Thursday
items.reason: Tuesday is mentioned first, then rejected. The final arrangement is Thursday.

items.evidence: The café upstairs is quieter
items.reason: The library is named but rejected.

items.prompt: Which article will speaker B use? First / second
items.evidence: the second one far clearer, and that's the one I'll use
items.reason: Speaker A's opinion is about the first article; the question asks about speaker B.

blocks.title: Spoken words and question words
blocks.mode: Guided classroom practice; no recording required
blocks.instructions: Match each spoken phrase (1-6) with the question wording (A-H) that means the same. Two options are not used.

stimulus.title: Question wording
paragraphs: A  cancel
C  not compulsory
D  register
E  interview in person
G  reasons for not doing something
H  limit the number

items.evidence: put my name down = register
items.reason: Both mean adding yourself to a list of participants.

items.prompt: we cap each day at twenty people
items.evidence: cap ... at twenty = limit the number
items.reason: To cap something is to set a maximum.

items.evidence: a quarter past nine = 9.15
items.reason: Quarter past means fifteen minutes after the hour. 9.45 is a quarter to ten.

items.prompt: talk to people face to face
items.evidence: face to face = in person
items.reason: Face to face means meeting directly, not online.

items.evidence: what stops = reasons for not doing
items.reason: Something that stops you is a reason you do not act.

items.prompt: you don't have to come to that part
items.evidence: don't have to = not compulsory
items.reason: Don't have to removes an obligation. It does not mean the event is cancelled.

blocks.support: Foundation: give learners the first answer as a worked example and allow a bilingual note beside each phrase. Record the support.
blocks.extension: Write a second paraphrase of your own for two of the phrases.

blocks.title: Volunteer weekend
blocks.mode: Guided listening practice: one play under practice conditions, then teacher-controlled review
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-4: complete the form. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Questions 5-6: choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

stimulus.title: Recording IELTS-05-L1 transcript (teacher-private)
paragraphs: RUTH: Riverside Community Garden, Ruth speaking.
DANIEL: Hello. I saw your notice about the volunteer weekend, and I'd like to put my name down.
RUTH: Lovely. Let me take a few details. Which day would you like to come? We run sessions on Saturday and Sunday.
DANIEL: Saturday would suit me best.
RUTH: Ah, I'm sorry, Saturday's already full. We cap each day at twenty people.
DANIEL: Oh. In that case, I'll come on Sunday.

RUTH: Sunday it is. Now, people often go to the library entrance, because that's where we met last year, but this time we're meeting at the north gate of the park. It's closer to the new vegetable beds.
DANIEL: The north gate. Got it.
RUTH: Do you have your own boots?
DANIEL: I don't, actually.
RUTH: That's fine. We provide boots in all sizes. What we can't provide this year is gloves, so please bring a pair.
DANIEL: Gloves. OK. And what time do we start?
RUTH: The leaflet says nine o'clock, but that's a mistake. We've moved it to a quarter past nine, so the tools can be unloaded first.
DANIEL: Nine fifteen, then.
RUTH: Can I ask what made you interested? It helps us place people.

DANIEL: Well, a couple of friends said it's a great way to meet people, and I suppose it's good exercise. But really, I'm studying environmental science, and I need some practical experience with soil and planting for my course.
RUTH: Perfect. I'll put you with our soil-testing group.
DANIEL: Great. Will you send me a map?
RUTH: There's a map on our website, so I won't post one. And the timetable for the day isn't finished yet. But I'll email you a safety form tonight. Please sign it and bring it on Sunday.
DANIEL: I will. Thanks very much.

items.evidence: In that case, I'll come on Sunday
items.reason: Saturday is his first choice but it is full.

items.prompt: Meeting point: the ________ of the park
items.evidence: this time we're meeting at the north gate of the park
items.reason: The library entrance was last year's meeting point.

items.evidence: What we can't provide this year is gloves, so please bring a pair
items.reason: Boots are provided, so they are not the answer.

items.evidence: We've moved it to a quarter past nine
items.reason: The leaflet time (nine o'clock) is corrected.

items.prompt: Daniel's main reason for volunteering is
options: B  to gain experience for his studies.
items.evidence: But really, I'm studying environmental science, and I need some practical experience
items.reason: Meeting people and exercise are mentioned, but 'But really' introduces his main reason.

items.evidence: I'll email you a safety form tonight
items.reason: The map is already online and the timetable is not finished.

blocks.support: Foundation: the workbook shows the answer type beside Questions 1-4. A second, paused play is allowed after the first attempt and is recorded as support.
blocks.extension: For Questions 5 and 6, write the words that made each wrong option tempting.
blocks.high_band: Before the review, write the signal phrase that introduced each correction or rejection (for example, 'In that case', 'but this time', 'but that's a mistake').

blocks.title: A research plan: cycling to campus
blocks.mode: Guided listening practice: one play under practice conditions, then teacher-controlled review
blocks.instructions: Questions 7-8: choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Questions 9-10: who expresses each view? Write L for Lena, M for Marco or P for Dr Price.

stimulus.title: Recording IELTS-05-L2 transcript (teacher-private)
paragraphs: DR PRICE: So, Lena and Marco, how's the cycling project going?
MARCO: Quite well. Our plan was to send an online questionnaire to all first-year students.
DR PRICE: Hmm. Online questionnaires often get very few replies in the first term. Have you thought about other options?
LENA: We did consider watching the main entrance and counting bikes, but we'd need to be there every morning for weeks.
DR PRICE: Yes, observation would take far too long for a project this size.
MARCO: So we've decided to talk to people face to face instead. We'll interview students at the bike racks outside the library.
DR PRICE: Good. Now, about your sample. You mentioned sixty students.
MARCO: I thought you were going to tell us that wasn't enough.
DR PRICE: No, sixty is fine for this stage. My concern is who those sixty people are. If you only speak to people who already cycle, you'll never find out what stops everyone else.
LENA: So we should include students who don't cycle at all.
DR PRICE: Exactly.
MARCO: For the questions, I think weather is the main reason people don't cycle. It rains so much here.
LENA: I'm not sure. When we tried our questions on ten classmates, most of them talked about feeling unsafe on the main road. Hardly anyone mentioned rain.
MARCO: Maybe, but ten people isn't many. I still think weather will come out on top.
DR PRICE: Well, that's exactly what your interviews can test. What about the final report?
MARCO: We'll include charts of the results. Somebody suggested a map of cycle routes as well, but I don't think it adds much.
DR PRICE: Actually, I'd like to see one. A map would show where the dangerous junctions are, which links directly to the safety question.
LENA: Then we'll need to decide who draws it.

items.prompt: How will the students now collect their data?
options: A  by interviewing students at bike racks
B  by sending an online questionnaire
C  by counting bikes at the main entrance
items.evidence: We'll interview students at the bike racks outside the library
items.reason: The questionnaire was the original plan; observation was considered and rejected.

items.prompt: What problem does Dr Price see with the sample?
options: B  It includes only people who cycle.
C  It was collected at one time of day.
items.evidence: If you only speak to people who already cycle, you'll never find out what stops everyone else
items.reason: Marco expects a comment about size, but Dr Price says sixty is fine.

items.prompt: Concerns about safety may matter more than the weather.
items.evidence: most of them talked about feeling unsafe on the main road. Hardly anyone mentioned rain
items.reason: Marco keeps his view about weather; Dr Price says the interviews can test it but takes no side.

items.prompt: A map would make the report more useful.
items.evidence: Actually, I'd like to see one. A map would show where the dangerous junctions are
items.reason: Marco mentions the map first but rejects it. Lena only asks who will draw it.

blocks.support: Foundation: before playing, the teacher reads the three speaker names aloud and learners write L, M and P in the margin.
blocks.extension: For Question 8, explain why option A is tempting, quoting Marco.
blocks.high_band: Explain in one sentence why Question 9 is not answered by Marco even though he talks about weather and safety.

stages.title: Opening challenge: the first answer is a trap
stages.student: Listen to three short lines read aloud and write only the final answer.
stages.teacher: Read each mini-model line once at natural speed. Students write before the reveal. Ask which word made the first answer wrong. This is a live mini-model, not an assessed recording.
stages.say: In IELTS Listening, the first thing you hear is not always the answer. Listen for the final decision.
stages.check: Most learners can name the word that signalled the change (then, so, but).

stages.title: Three distractor patterns and paraphrase
stages.student: Complete the paraphrase matching in the workbook alone (4 minutes), then check with the reveal.
stages.teacher: Teach the three patterns from the mini-model: correction, rejected option, contrasting opinion. Then run the matching task. Reveal answers only after learners commit. Stress that question wording rarely repeats the recording.
stages.say: The recording and the question say the same thing in different words. Your job is to hear the meaning.
stages.check: Learners can explain Q3 (quarter past) and Q6 (don't have to).

stages.title: Prepare for Recording 1
stages.student: Read Questions 1-6. Predict the type of answer for each gap.
stages.teacher: Give 30 seconds' reading time inside the recording plus up to 2 minutes of prediction. Do not pre-teach the answers. Foundation learners use the printed answer-type hints.
stages.say: Before you listen, decide: is the answer a day, a place, a thing or a time?
stages.check: Each learner has written a prediction beside at least two gaps.

stages.title: Recording 1: one play
stages.student: Listen once and answer Questions 1-6. Keep your first answers.
stages.teacher: Play IELTS-05-L1 once without pausing. Do not repeat or react to answers. If audio fails, stop and use Plan B; never read the transcript as a substitute for this practice play.
stages.say: You will hear the recording once. Write as you listen.
stages.check: All learners have committed answers before the review.

stages.title: Review Recording 1 and trap analysis
stages.student: Compare your answers with the reveal. Mark the trap you fell into, without erasing your first answer.
stages.teacher: Reveal answers in pairs. For each, ask what was said first and what changed it. Optional: a teacher-controlled second play with pauses for foundation learners, recorded as support. Corrections remain guided practice.
stages.say: Boots, nine o'clock and the library were all in the recording. Why were they wrong?
stages.check: Learners can name the trap type for Q1, Q2 and Q4.

stages.title: Prepare for Recording 2
stages.student: Read Questions 7-10. Underline the key idea in each option.
stages.teacher: Point out the three speaker names. Explain that in matching tasks you match the view to the person who actually says it, not the person who mentions the topic.
stages.say: Three people, different opinions. Listen for who agrees and who disagrees.
stages.check: Learners have written L, M and P beside Questions 9-10.

stages.title: Recording 2: one play
stages.teacher: Play IELTS-05-L2 once without pausing. Note interruptions or learners arriving late.
stages.say: Listen for changes of plan and for who holds each view.

stages.title: Review Recording 2: who said it?
stages.student: Check answers. For Questions 9-10, write the speaker's exact words that prove the answer.
stages.teacher: Reveal Q7-Q8, then Q9-Q10. Model the reasoning for Q10: Marco mentions the map but rejects it; Dr Price supports it. Extension and high-band learners complete their written tasks from the workbook.
stages.say: Mentioning an idea is not the same as agreeing with it.
stages.check: Learners explain Q10 using the word 'Actually'.

stages.title: My error log
stages.student: Complete the error log at the end of the workbook: for each wrong answer, name the trap type and the signal you missed. Choose one target.
stages.teacher: Circulate. Note the trap types learners actually record. Do not convert raw scores from these guided tasks to bands.
stages.say: Your error log tells us what to practise next, not your IELTS score.
stages.check: Each learner has one target written in their own words.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket. Take the homework sheet.
stages.teacher: Collect exit tickets. Assign online practice only through the existing workflow, and only where a reviewed task is eligible. Record a follow-up date for the withheld fresh check.
stages.say: Next lesson we will read for specific information, using the same idea: find the meaning, not the matching word.
stages.check: Everyone knows the homework and the next check date.

exit_ticket: One trap pattern I can now recognise:
A signal word that told me the speaker changed their mind:
My target for the next listening task:
homework: Paraphrase notebook: write five pairs of phrases that mean the same (for example, 'put my name down' / 'register'). Use phrases from today or from English you hear this week.
Re-read your error log. For one wrong answer, write what you would listen for next time.

Complete only the Brains Heist listening practice your teacher actually assigns. A printed instruction does not create an online assignment. Suggested time: about 25 minutes, adjusted by your teacher.

followup.status: Private fresh-transfer draft. Withhold from advance student distribution. Recording not produced. Human review and exposure/comparability checks pending.
followup.delivery: About one teaching week after Lesson 5, once the recording is approved. Play once without pausing, no transcript, no coaching, after 30 seconds of reading time. Log support, interruptions and prior exposure. Classroom observation only unless separately approved for stronger claims.

blocks.title: Summer placement at the City Museum
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-4: complete the notes. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Questions 5-6: choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

stimulus.title: Recording IELTS-05-C1 transcript (teacher-private)
paragraphs: SAM: City Museum, education office. Sam speaking.
AISHA: Hi. I'm calling about the summer work placement. I've been offered a place, and I need to confirm a few details.
SAM: Congratulations. Could I take your name?
AISHA: Aisha Karimova. That's K, A, R, I, M, O, V, A.
SAM: Thank you. Right, you'll be working in the education department. Actually, no, sorry, I've just checked, and you're with the archive team this year.
AISHA: The archive. That sounds interesting.
SAM: The placement lasts three weeks. Most people start on the first of July, but your start date is the eighth of July, because the archive is closed for repairs in the first week.
AISHA: And where should I go on my first day?
SAM: Not the main reception. It gets very crowded in summer. Please come to the staff entrance on Mill Street.
AISHA: Do I need to bring anything?
SAM: You'll get a uniform on the day, and lunch is provided. Just bring your passport. A student card isn't accepted for security reasons.
AISHA: What will I mostly be doing?
SAM: Some people expect to give tours, but placements don't do that. You'll mainly be scanning old photographs so they can go online, and occasionally helping at weekend family events.
AISHA: Will I be paid?
SAM: It's unpaid, I'm afraid, but we cover your bus fares, and you'll get a reference letter at the end.

items.evidence: you're with the archive team this year
items.reason: The education department is corrected.

items.evidence: your start date is the eighth of July
items.reason: The first of July applies to most people, not Aisha.

items.prompt: First day: go to the ________ on Mill Street
items.evidence: Please come to the staff entrance on Mill Street
items.reason: The main reception is rejected.

items.evidence: Just bring your passport
items.reason: A student card is not accepted; the uniform and lunch are provided.

items.evidence: You'll mainly be scanning old photographs
items.reason: Tours are ruled out; family events are only occasional.

items.evidence: we cover your bus fares
items.reason: The placement is unpaid; membership is not mentioned.

followup.review: Compare only the observed response demand and conditions with Lesson 5 work. Record what the new work shows, counterevidence and the next check. A fresh script does not by itself establish comparable difficulty or improvement. No percentage, band or mastery cutoff.

delayed_followup: Two to three teaching weeks later, include one distractor item in a different context (for example, Lesson 10 or 14 materials) and check whether the learner still waits for the final decision without prompting. Record it as a later observation, not proof of retention.
mapping_notes: Proposed focuses use Diagnostic Bible section 7.1 construct names. They are draft teaching focuses, not approved taxonomy mappings, and items from one recording are not independent longitudinal observations.
